svg.title: The EMORI adapter architecture: the Pokamind session feed, the hostapp hub, the five-node ROS 2 / ROS4HRI graph, the FIWARE chain and the robot
svg.desc: A Pokamind session emits an analysis cycle about every two seconds and one event per spoken sentence. The kiosk page relays each envelope to the hostapp, which stamps the session identity and fans it out to the in-process driver, the recorder and the /ws/relay broadcast. The emori_adapter node reads that broadcast and publishes three standard REP-155 person topics plus two EMORI extensions, Context and SpeechCue. A context analyzer splits Context into single-purpose topics, an engagement node names a bounded motion on the /skill lane, and a FIWARE bridge historizes to NGSI-LD. Only skill_facade runs a request, and it does so by posting to the hostapp, which owns the single robot queue.

g.text: From a Pokamind session to ROS4HRI signals, robot behaviour and FIWARE analytics
The ROS 2 graph works out what the robot should do. The hostapp is the only component that moves it.

text.tspan: asks for it by name. It holds
the only node that runs a
Figure 1. The EMORI adapter architecture. Blue: the Pokamind session that supplies the analysis feed, and the kiosk page that hosts it. Amber: the emori-hostapp,
which stamps the session identity onto every envelope, fans it out to three consumers, and owns the single queue that moves the robot. Violet: the ROS 2 graph,
five nodes in one container on a local DDS domain. Teal: standard REP-155 topics. Rose: the two EMORI message extensions and the bounded skill lane. Green: the
FIWARE analytics chain. Grey: the Reachy daemon and the robot itself.
No node in the ROS graph holds a daemon URL. The graph works out what the robot should do, and skill_facade asks for it over HTTP, so one queue keeps its ordering
and its interlocks. The ROS person namespace is the stable person_id parameter, because the robot serves one learner at a time; the real per-session identity travels
inside emori_msgs/Context. A sixth executable, pyhri_demo, is built but not launched: it reads the same topics through hri.HRIListener to show that standard ROS4HRI
tooling picks the graph up unchanged.
